Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme wants to move to a short hands-on POC focused on routing policy and load behaviour. High-level asks: prompt review + instruction tuning checks, model selection (latency vs quality), fallback rules, regional routing (eu/us), and a short load run (50k tokens/min sustained for 10–15m) to validate autoscaling.

Suggested duration: 2 hours (working session + 30m buffer). Our proposed dates: Apr 18 or Apr 19 (morning CET). Attendees from our side: me (technical lead) and Tim Park (infra contact, cc'd when confirmed).

Can you confirm:
- Preferred date/time options (we're flexible but prefer CET mornings)
- Whether Redwood can reserve dedicated capacity for the load run and provide network whitelist details we need to open
- A draft agenda so we can align internally

I'll attach a CSV with our expected workload distribution.

Thanks,
Sarah

Head of ML Ops, Acme AI

Thanks Hannah — a few internal notes for the session planning (blocking items):

1) Model selection: recommend we present two baseline variants:
   - rw-medium-qa-v1 (balanced latency/quality) as primary
   - rw-small-q4 (low-latency fallback) for traffic tiering/fallback tests
   We'll bring performance profiles (p50/p95) and cost estimates per 1k tokens.

2) Fallback rules: propose a policy example during the workshop:
   - prefer rw-medium for high-confidence prompts
   - if latency > 250ms or error rate > 1% for 30s, switch to rw-small gracefully
   - cross-region fallback to US-only pool if EU pool is saturated (with notification)

3) Load run: we should reserve 3 x gpus for the first 15m and a warmup phase. Connor, can you confirm capacity reservation and provide a reservation id?

4) Telemetry: Laura, please prep the dashboard links and the tracing hook we'll use to show token-level latency and KV cache hit rates.

I'll draft a short slide with the policy examples to walk through.

-Marcus
